title: How it ends is how it felt
text: Ask people how much a painful experience hurt, and their answer {{1}} little relation to the total. In one study, patients undergoing a medical procedure {{2}} their discomfort minute by minute; those whose ordeal was made longer by three extra minutes of mild discomfort remembered it as less painful than those who stopped at the worse moment. Memory, it turns out, does not {{3}} experience like a video recorder. It keeps two {{4}}: how bad it got at the worst point, and how it felt at the end. Everything else — duration above all — is largely {{5}}. The peak-end rule, as psychologists call it, {{6}} far beyond the clinic: how a holiday is remembered depends on its best moment and its final hours, not its average day, and a concert that {{7}} badly is remembered as a failure. The rule {{8}} anyone who can choose endings: a little kindness at the close buys more remembered happiness than hours of mediocrity in the middle. Duration neglect also explains a curious truth — we do not regret long, mildly unpleasant experiences more than short ones, though we surely lived them longer.

gaps.explanation: 'their answer bears little relation to the total' — 'bear relation to' is the fixed phrase; wear and lend do not collocate, and 'shares' would need 'in common'.
'patients rated their discomfort minute by minute' — scored it; race = run, root = fix in place.
'memory does not record experience like a video recorder' — store it faithfully; recite = repeat aloud from memory.
'it keeps two measurements' — the worst point and the end, both recorded; secrets, promises and souvenirs are not kept by a memory acting as a gauge.
'duration is largely ignored' — disregarded; inundate = flood, and 'illuded' is not standard English (deluded).
'the rule reaches far beyond the clinic' — extends its influence; roam = wander, rattle = shake noisily.
'a concert that finishes badly' — comes to an end badly; furnish = equip, languish = decline sadly.
'the rule concerns anyone who can choose endings' — applies to and matters for; conceal = hide, corrupt = make dishonest.
